newsitem.title: USA: U.S. foreign crudes tighten on supply woes.
newsitem.headline: U.S. foreign crudes tighten on supply woes.

text.p: U.S. foreign crude activity tightened on Thursday as refiners sought to cover indefinite delays in Cano Limon loadings and the possible effects of a storm in the Gulf of Mexico, traders said.
A U.S. company was offering North Sea Brent crude for August 25-30 delivery at 15 cents under West Texas Intermediate/Cushing, up 10 cents from earlier in the week.

At least one other company was eyeing the possibility of bringing more Brent into the Gulf. "We're looking at it, but it's still too early to be firm about it," a seller said. "I think the arb is very narrow."
Among other North Sea grades, a Norwegian company sold Heidrun crude to a U.S. refiner apparently seeking to cover ongoing delays in Cano Limon loadings.
The cargo was sold around $1.00 a barrel under September WTI/Cushing for mid-August delivery to the Gulf Coast.
Colombian Cano Limon crude liftings have been subject to force majeure since July 6 after a string of rebel bombings of the pipeline that carries the crude to the Caribbean port of Covenas.
Operator Occidental also declared force majeure on the field itself, the first time Oxy has ever taken such as action in Colombia.
Pipeline repairs were expected to begin late on Thursday.
Meanwhile, equity producer Total sold a cargo of Colombian Cusiana crude at an undisclosed discount to October WTI/Cushing for August 27-31 loading.
The gasoline-rich grade changed hands twice on Wednesday at October WTI/Cushing minus 82 cents a barrel.
Traders said one cargo of Cusiana remains in August. Colombian state oil company Ecopetrol is soliciting bids for a cargo loading August 19-23.
Elsewhere in the region, Chile's state oil refiner Empresa Nacional del Petroleo (ENAP) bought Angolan Palanca and Ecuadoran Oriente crude cargoes in its latest purchase tender, trade sources said.
The cargoes are scheduled to be delivered in the September 1-4 window.
A Swiss-based trading house sold 380,000 barrels of Oriente to ENAP at an undisclosed discount to West Texas Intermediate/Cushing, trade sources said.
A European company sold 950,000-960,000 barrels of Palanca to ENAP at a premium to Dated Brent.
The Chilean company purchased the same combination of crudes in its last tender for August delivery.
